items.title: George Wein interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I played with Buck Clayton and Vic Dickinson and Doc Cheatham and Buddy Tate

ctx.x: Do you have an idea why, for that stretch of time, well for too long, that drugs were so much connected with jazz and so much a part of it?

I don’t have any story about why it was. I don’t know. And I’m not a sociologist in any way. I do know that prior to Charlie Parker, marijuana was — because Louis Armstrong was a big influence on people smoking marijuana. Alcohol was a very big thing with musicians. A lot of musicians were heavy into alcohol — Pee Wee Russell or Vic Dickinson or J.C. Higginbotham, all the guys with Basie’s band and Dickie Wells. They were real alcoholics. And so there is something about the music business and the lack of…
Okay. I brought a little piece of music to play for you. It might jog your memory.
